claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have Alex, who's 4 years old.

Now, let me ask you some questions to assess eligibility. First, I need to understand your living situation:

**Does Alex currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex does live with me, yes. But I should mention that their other parent also lives with us in the same house.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It's good to know that Alex lives with you and their other parent in the same house.

I now need to check some key eligibility criteria. Let me ask:

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have a right to reside in the UK?** This includes being a British citizen, having settled status, or having the right to reside under UK immigration rules.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK resident. I live in Birmingham and I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. That helps with the residency requirement.

Now I need to understand the living arrangements a bit better:

**Is Alex's other parent also a British citizen or UK resident with the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they are. They're also a UK resident with the right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's useful context.

Now I need to ask an important question about who will be claiming Child Benefit:

**Will you be the one claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or will Alex's other parent be claiming it?** (Note: typically only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, even if both parents live in the same household.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Well, actually, Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

I need to ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**How old is Alex currently, and has Alex reached their 16th birthday yet?** (I want to confirm the exact age to ensure they still fall within the eligible age range for Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 4 years old, so no, they haven't reached their 16th birthday yet - they're still quite young!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming Alex's age. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me read the official eligibility criteria to ensure I give you the correct outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official eligibility criteria I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

**The key issue here is:** According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you cannot also claim it for the same child.

The rules clearly state: "Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child" and "Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child."

While Alex does meet the basic eligibility criteria (under 16, lives in the UK with you, and you're a UK resident), you cannot receive Child Benefit because the other parent has already claimed it.

If there are any changes to your circumstances (for example, if the other parent stops claiming), you could potentially claim it then. Otherwise, you would need to contact HMRC to discuss your specific situation if you believe there's been a mistake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time. While Alex would normally qualify (being under 16 and living with you in the UK), the fundamental issue is that only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child, and Alex's other parent is already claiming it.

If your circumstances change in the future, or if you'd like to discuss this further, I'd recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly.
